title: Signal Enrichment Pipeline for Sales/CS Enterprise Requests — Economic & Compliance Anchors
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Background: Sales and Customer Success teams receive high-touch enterprise feature requests that frequently lack the business context or compliance classification necessary for quick scoping. This creates long back-and-forths, uneven prioritization, and missed signal for product roadmaps. Goal: Build a lightweight enrichment pipeline that transforms raw Sales/CS requests into a standardized request object with: 1) economic proxies (ARR opportunity band, estimated dev cost bucket), 2) compliance flags (data residency, PII, regulated industry), 3) implementation-readiness score (0-10) and 4) mapping to likely technical owners or required infra changes. The output will be used by PMs for faster first-pass scoping and by the prioritization engine to rank tickets by expected business value and implementation effort. Scope: - Input formats: email, Zendesk/SFDC snippets, and manual intake form entries submitted by CS. - Enrichment steps: automated pattern extraction (NLP), lookups (customer account tier, recent contract value), and a short manual validate flow for ambiguous entries. - Deliverables: enrichment microservice (API), a scoring rubric, UI preview in intake console, and a short handbook for Sales/CS. Out of scope: full automated ROI calculation, full legal sign-off workflows, and replacing deep forensic compliance reviews.
acceptance_criteria: Enrichment API accepts raw request payload and returns standardized JSON with economic_band, compliance_flags, readiness_score, suggested_owner_tags in >= 90% of test cases.
Automated lookup integrates with CRM to attach account_tier and latest_contract_value metadata for 95% of enterprise accounts in test dataset.
Scorecard rubric defined and reviewed by PMs and Security with documented thresholds for 'High touch follow-up' and 'Auto-queue for backlog'.
Intake Console UI shows enrichment preview and allows Sales/CS to mark 'Needs more info'; audit trail recorded for subsequent changes.
A baseline evaluation run on last 6 months of closed requests shows the pipeline correctly prioritizes top 20% of revenue-impacting asks in 80% of cases.

risks_and_mitigations: Risk: CRM lookups miss accounts with multiple aliases -> Mitigation: add heuristics and manual override in UI.
Risk: Readiness score too noisy leading to mistrust by PMs -> Mitigation: conservative thresholds and gradual calibration via pilot feedback.
Risk: Compliance flags trigger unnecessary legal reviews -> Mitigation: use triage-level flags (informational vs blocking) and require Security sign-off only for 'blocking' flags.
Risk: Sales adoption low if enrichment requires extra steps -> Mitigation: keep default path automated and provide lightweight correction UI rather than mandatory fields.
open_questions: Q1: Which CRM field is the canonical 'ARR' proxy? Finance favors 'contract_value_monthly' but Sales often updates 'forecasted_ARR'. Decision needed.
Q2: Is compliance flagging allowed to persist in customer-visible artifacts? Ops prefers internal-only; Product suggests visibility for Sales to prep messaging.
Q3: How should multi-account opportunities (MKA) be represented in economic_band? Flatten to highest ARR or tag multiple accounts?
Q4: What SLA should the enrichment API meet for synchronous intake (<=300ms) vs asynchronous batch enrichment?
